scope: Amazon RDS usage covered by a Database Savings Plan, 1-year term
claim: Amazon RDS usage can be covered by Database Savings Plans, which reduce costs by up to 35% for a commitment to a consistent amount of usage over a 1-year term.
q: Is Amazon RDS covered by Database Savings Plans, and what discount do they give?
ev: f
Yes, you can purchase a Database Savings Plans for your Amazon RDS usage and reduce your costs by up to 35% when you commit to a consistent amount of usage over a 1-year term.
note: Database Savings Plans are recent; the decisions+changes lens must check the launch date against the 'not examinable yet' rule (GA after 2026-07-15).

claim: Partial DB instance hours are billed in one-second increments, with a 10 minute minimum charge after a billable status change such as creating, starting or modifying the DB instance class.
q: How are partial Amazon RDS DB instance hours billed?
ev: f

Partial DB instance hours consumed are billed in one-second increments with a 10 minute minimum charge following a billable status change, such as creating, starting, or modifying the DB instance class.

claim: DB instance hours are billed for each hour the DB instance runs in an available state; to stop paying instance hours you must stop or delete it.
q: What must you do to stop paying Amazon RDS DB instance hours?
ev: f

DB instance hours are billed for each hour your DB instance is running in an available state. If you no longer wish to be charged for your DB instance, you must stop or delete it to avoid being billed for additional instance hours.

claim: A stopped DB instance is still charged for provisioned storage (including Provisioned IOPS) and backup storage, but not for DB instance hours.
q: What do you pay for while an Amazon RDS DB instance is stopped?
d: but not for DB instance hours
ev: f

While your database instance is stopped, you are charged for provisioned storage (including Provisioned IOPS) and backup storage (including manual snapshots and automated backups within your specified retention window), but not for DB instance hours.

claim: With Provisioned IOPS (SSD) storage you pay per month for the provisioned IOPS rate, regardless of the IOPS you consume.
q: How is Provisioned IOPS billed on Amazon RDS?
ev: f
Provisioned IOPS per month – Provisioned IOPS rate, regardless of IOPS consumed (for Amazon RDS Provisioned IOPS (SSD) Storage only)

claim: Free backup storage is provided up to the account's total provisioned database storage in the Region; only backup storage above that is charged.
q: How much Amazon RDS backup storage is free?
ev: f
Free backup storage is provided up to your account's total provisioned database storage across the entire region.
f
Please note that the free backup storage is account-specific and region-specific.

claim: Backup size is directly proportional to the amount of data on the DB instance; after the first backup, backups are incremental and store only changed data.
q: How large are Amazon RDS backups?
ev: f
Subsequent backups are incremental, and will only store the changed data on your DB instance.
f
The size of your backups are directly proportional to the amount of data on your instance.

claim: DB instance storage for primary data is in a single Availability Zone, but backup data (including transaction logs) is replicated across multiple Availability Zones.
q: Where is Amazon RDS backup data stored compared with the DB instance storage?
ev: f

The storage provisioned to your DB instance for your primary data is located within a single Availability Zone. When your database is backed up, the backup data (including transactions logs) is geo-redundantly replicated across multiple Availability Zones to provide even greater levels of data durability.

claim: In a Multi-AZ DB instance deployment, write I/O for database updates doubles because RDS replicates synchronously to the standby; read I/O stays the same.
q: How does a Multi-AZ deployment change Amazon RDS I/O usage?
d: Read I/O usage will remain the same
ev: f
Write I/O usage associated with database updates will double as Amazon RDS synchronously replicates your data to the standby DB instance. Read I/O usage will remain the same.

claim: You are not charged for data transfer used to replicate data between the Multi-AZ primary and standby.
q: Is data transfer between a Multi-AZ primary and standby charged?
d: You are not charged for the data transfer
ev: f
Data transfer – You are not charged for the data transfer incurred in replicating data between your primary and standby.

claim: Backup storage usage is the same for a standard and a Multi-AZ deployment; in Multi-AZ, backups are taken from the standby.
q: Does Multi-AZ change Amazon RDS backup storage usage?
ev: f

Backup Storage – Your backup storage usage will not change whether your DB instance is a standard or Multi-AZ deployment. Backups will simply be taken from your standby to avoid I/O suspension on the DB instance primary.

claim: RDS reserved instances reserve a DB instance for a one or three year term in exchange for a significant discount compared to On-Demand pricing.
q: What terms do Amazon RDS reserved instances have?
ev: f

Amazon RDS reserved instances give you the option to reserve a DB instance for a one or three year term and in turn receive a significant discount compared to the on-demand instance pricing for the DB instance.

claim: Reserved instances have three payment options: No Upfront, Partial Upfront and All Upfront.
q: Which payment options do Amazon RDS reserved instances have?
d: No Upfront, Partial Upfront, All Upfront
ev: f
There are three RI payment options -- No Upfront, Partial Upfront, All Upfront -- which enable you to balance the amount you pay upfront with your effective hourly price.

claim: RDS reserved instances are bought for a Region, not an Availability Zone, so they are not capacity reservations.
q: Does an Amazon RDS reserved instance reserve capacity?
ev: f
Amazon RDS reserved instances are purchased for a Region rather than for a specific Availability Zone. As RIs are not specific to an Availability Zone, they are not capacity reservations.

claim: You cannot cancel an RDS reserved DB instance, and the one-time payment (if any) is not refundable.
q: Can you cancel an Amazon RDS reserved instance?
d: you cannot cancel your reserved DB instance
ev: f
No, you cannot cancel your reserved DB instance and the one-time payment (if applicable) is not refundable.

claim: A reserved instance is tied to one Region for its whole term and cannot be moved, but it can be used in any Availability Zone of that Region.
q: Can you move an Amazon RDS reserved instance to another Region?
d: fixed for the lifetime of the reservation
ev: f

Each reserved instance is associated with a specific Region, which is fixed for the lifetime of the reservation and cannot be changed. Each reservation can, however, be used in any of the available AZs within the associated Region.

claim: Reserved instances are available for Multi-AZ deployments: you select the Multi-AZ option when you buy the reservation.
q: Are Amazon RDS reserved instances available for Multi-AZ deployments?
ev: f
When you purchase a reserved instance, you can select the Multi-AZ option in the DB instance configuration available for purchase.

cond: engine and license model that support reserved instance size flexibility
claim: With an engine and license model that support size flexibility, a Multi-AZ reserved instance covers usage for two Single-AZ DB instances.
q: How much Single-AZ usage does a size-flexible Multi-AZ RDS reserved instance cover?
ev: f
In addition, if you are using a DB engine and license model that supports reserved instance size-flexibility, a Multi-AZ reserved instance will cover usage for two Single-AZ DB instances.

claim: A DB instance reservation can apply to a read replica when the DB instance class and Region are the same.
q: Can an Amazon RDS reserved instance cover a read replica?
ev: f
A DB instance reservation can be applied to a read replica, provided the DB instance class and Region are the same.

claim: For engines eligible for size flexibility (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora, Oracle Bring Your Own License), a reservation applies to a running DB instance of any size in the same instance family, engine and Region.
q: Which Amazon RDS reservations are size-flexible?
d: any size within the same instance family
ev: f

A reservation for a DB engine and license model that is eligible for size-flexibility (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Amazon Aurora, or Oracle "Bring Your Own License") will automatically apply to a running DB instance of any size within the same instance family (e.g. M4, T2, or R3) for the same database engine and Region.

claim: Allocated storage can be increased while the DB instance stays available.
q: Does an RDS DB instance stay available while you increase its storage?
ev: f
The storage capacity allocated to your DB Instance can be increased while maintaining DB Instance availability.

claim: Changing the DB instance class makes the database temporarily unavailable, typically for a few minutes, during the maintenance window unless the change is applied immediately.
q: Does an RDS DB instance stay available while you change its instance class?
ev: f

However, when you decide to scale the compute resources available to your DB instance up or down, your database will be temporarily unavailable while the DB instance class is modified. This period of unavailability typically lasts only a few minutes, and will occur during the maintenance window for your DB Instance, unless you specify that the modification should be applied immediately.

claim: Instance class and storage changes are applied in the maintenance window unless you use the apply-immediately flag, which also applies any other pending system changes.
q: What else happens when you apply an RDS scaling change immediately?
ev: f

Please note that when you modify your DB Instance class or allocated storage, your requested changes will be applied during your specified maintenance window. Alternately, you can use the “apply-immediately” flag to apply your scaling requests immediately. Bear in mind that any other pending system changes will be applied as well.
